reasons: Both meet all four rubric items: each says to send tonight because today is the last day, neither offers the hour or office hours as a reason to hold, and both code blocks give a complete placeholder notice naming the ceiling leak on the 3rd. B wins on secondary quality by putting the deadline correction before the deliverable instead of after it, and by separating notice from claim so the user's wish for fresh eyes is redirected to the inventory and estimates rather than left unanswered. B also handles uncertainty better (keep the timestamped sent copy, do not assert a policy period it cannot verify, do not understate the damage), where A is leaner but buries the timing push below the block.
